in_english.name: Agate
in_english.long_meaning: Agate is a name of excellence, virtue, or nobility derived from the Greek word αγγελλενγτε, which signifies strength, virtue, and nobility. In Christian tradition, Agate is associated with moral excellence, courage, and perseverance. It is also linked to the Greek concept of arete, which encompasses virtues such as wisdom, courage, and justice. As a given name, Agate conveys a sense of high moral character, integrity, and strength of character.

data.cultural_impact: Agate has been cherished as a gemstone since ancient times. Aside from its physical beauty, Agate was believed to possess various magical and healing properties. Different cultures revered Agate for its believed ability to strengthen, stabilize, protection, and promote strength and endurance. It has been used as an ornament and as a symbol of wealth and status, particularly during the Roman period when Agates were often set into jewelry and architecture as decoration.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, Agate represents the connection between the Spiritual and the material worlds. It symbolizes the virtues of patience, endurance, and purity, and is believed to offer protection against negative influences. The stone is also associated with consecration, spirituality, and wholeness in the Christian faith. Wearing Agate jewelry or carrying an Agate stone is believed to bring peace, harmony, and balance both physically and spiritually.
